key_insight: OpenMedReason adds large-scale, human-authored medical reasoning supervision so vision-language models learn not just answers, but grounded rationales tied to visual evidence and clinical knowledge.
clinical_relevance: This could improve medical AI reliability by making model outputs more interpretable and better aligned with the evidence clinicians use when judging images.
method: Built a ~450K-instance multimodal corpus with image-question-answer pairs and curated reasoning traces from biomedical scientific articles.
Covered diverse medical imaging modalities, including radiology, microscopy, visible-light photos, charts, and more.
Added OpenMedReason-Bench to evaluate perception, medical knowledge, and rationale separately.
evidence_signal: Training with OpenMedReason improved VQA accuracy by 20% on average, landed within 4.2% of the strongest comparable medical LVLMs, and had reasoning traces preferred in 86.1% of pairwise comparisons.
watch_item: Because the corpus relies on curated article-derived reasoning, performance gains may not fully transfer to real-world clinical settings without careful external validation.
paper_title: OpenMedReason: Scientific Reasoning Supervision for Medical Vision-Language Models
